scope.scopeNotesMd: This report compares the core primitive datatype `string` StructureDefinition in R4 4.0.1 with the R6 6.0.0-ballot4 counterpart. The canonical URL, id, name, kind, type, status, abstract flag, and snapshot element set were compared directly. The direct `baseDefinition` changed from `Element` to `PrimitiveType`, but that reflects the R6 datatype hierarchy (`Element` -> `DataType` -> `PrimitiveType`) and is treated as inherited/base-infrastructure scope, not as a local `string` finding.
outOfScope: R6 introduction/use of `DataType` and `PrimitiveType` as intermediate base artifacts for primitive datatypes, including the resulting `string.baseDefinition` change from `Element` to `PrimitiveType`.
Inherited `Element` constraint wording change for `ele-1` from 'All FHIR elements must have a @value or children' to 'All FHIR elements must have a @value or children or both'.
Removal of inherited XPath expressions from constraints supplied by base artifacts such as `Element` and `Extension`.
Inherited `Element.id`, `Element.extension`, slicing, and extension-governance text changes that are assessed in base artifact reports.
Terminology expansion analysis; `string` has no local terminology binding to expand.

narrativeReportMd:
# string R4->R6 breaking-change assessment

## Bottom line
No hard R4-to-R6 instance-breaking change was found for the local `string` datatype. The one local material delta is a broadened `string.value` regex, which primarily creates an R6-to-R4 representability and old-validator compatibility risk for rare string values containing whitespace/control characters not accepted by the R4 regex.

## Scope
The analysis covered the R4 and R6 core `StructureDefinition/string` files, package metadata, package indexes, and relevant base StructureDefinitions only to separate inherited hierarchy changes from local `string` changes. Base hierarchy movement through `DataType` and `PrimitiveType`, inherited constraint wording, and inherited XPath removal are not counted as local findings.

## Main migration themes
The element model is stable: `string`, `string.id`, `string.extension`, and `string.value` remain present with unchanged cardinalities, representations, max length, modifier flags, and summary flags. The practical issue is validator behavior around the primitive value regex.

## Highest-impact findings
There are no Critical or High local findings. The Medium finding is `string:VALUE_CONSTRAINT:string.value:regex-broadened`: R6 accepts any non-empty character sequence using `^[\s\S]+$`, while R4 used `[ \r\n\t\S]+`.

## Findings requiring human review
Human review is useful for the regex finding because exact runtime impact depends on validator regex dialect, whether validation uses whole-string matching, and whether a deployment also applies JSON/XML character restrictions outside the StructureDefinition regex.

## Backward-compatible design observations
The regex broadening appears aligned with the stated definition 'A sequence of Unicode characters' and is not R4-to-R6 breaking. A less disruptive cross-version posture would have been explanatory guidance or warnings for characters not round-trippable to R4, but preserving the older regex would continue to exclude some Unicode/control whitespace despite the broader definition.

## Follow-up analysis
Assess the `Element`, `DataType`, and `PrimitiveType` reports for the R6 class-hierarchy and inherited constraint changes that affect all datatypes, including `string`.

summary.executiveSummaryMd: No local hard R4-to-R6 break was found for `string`. The main migration concern is the widened `string.value` regex, which can make some R6-valid strings fail R4 validators or cross-version round-trips. The main uncertainty is the exact impact across regex engines and serializer-level character rules.
summary.migrationThemesMd: Migration is mostly validator and conformance tooling work rather than data reshaping. Existing R4 data that passed the old regex should continue to pass the R6 regex, but systems that down-convert R6 content to R4 or reuse R4-generated validators must decide how to handle values accepted only by the R6 regex. The R6 base hierarchy change should be handled in base datatype infrastructure, not as a `string`-specific migration.
summary.confidenceSummaryMd: Confidence is high for the structural comparison because the assigned R4 and R6 StructureDefinitions are present and the local element/cardinality/type/flag deltas are directly computable. Confidence is medium for the practical prevalence of the regex issue because behavior depends on regex dialect, whole-match semantics, and additional JSON/XML character constraints.

findings.title: string.value regex broadened from selected whitespace plus non-whitespace to any non-empty character sequence

oldState.narrativeMd: The R4 primitive value regex allowed one or more characters that were either space, carriage return, line feed, tab, or matched `\S` in the validator's regex dialect.

newState.summary: R6 `string.value` uses regex `^[\s\S]+$` with the same maxLength 1048576.
newState.narrativeMd: The R6 primitive value regex explicitly anchors a one-or-more-character pattern that accepts either whitespace or non-whitespace, which is effectively any non-empty string under normal regex semantics.

facts.note: The regex was broadened and anchored.
The maximum length did not change.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: `string.value` has the same element id and path in both StructureDefinitions; only the regex extension value changed.

impact.impactRationaleMd: This is not a hard R4-to-R6 validation break because the R6 regex is broader than the R4 regex for normal whole-string validation. The risk is in the reverse direction: an R6 instance can contain a non-empty string value that the old R4 regex would reject, especially for whitespace/control characters outside R4's explicit space/CR/LF/tab set. Runtime risk is mostly limited to validators, generated schemas, and conversion pipelines that keep using the R4 regex against R6 content.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: The issue is unlikely to create direct clinical safety risk by itself, but rejected or normalized narrative text could cause data loss in downstream systems if conversion errors are not surfaced.

justification.inferredGoal: Align the primitive string lexical rule with the broad definition 'A sequence of Unicode characters' and remove exclusions caused by the older character class.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Not applicable: the regex broadening preserves R4-valid strings in R6 and is not an R4-to-R6 base-design break.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The local evidence shows `string.value` was broadened from `[ \r\n\t\S]+` to `^[\s\S]+$` while cardinality and max length stayed unchanged. That inferred goal is reasonable for a datatype defined as a sequence of Unicode characters, and the change does not invalidate R4-valid instances in R6. The remaining compatibility cost is reverse-direction: R6 can now permit uncommon characters that R4 validators may reject. Because no official change rationale was available locally, `Probably justified` is more appropriate than an unqualified `Justified`.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: No backward-compatible base-design alternative is needed for R4-to-R6 compatibility because the R6 rule is a widening, not a narrowing. A conservative alternative would have retained the R4 regex and added narrative clarification or warnings, but that would fail the apparent R6 goal of accepting the full non-empty character space described by the datatype. Cross-version guidance remains useful as mitigation for R6-to-R4 conversion, but that is not a less-breaking base R6 design alternative.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Keeping the R4 regex would improve R6-to-R4 validator compatibility but would preserve older exclusions and narrow the intended R6 lexical space.

examples.examplesMd: The example is illustrative rather than a complete FHIR instance. A vertical-tab character is accepted by `^[\s\S]+$` in common regex engines but is outside R4's explicit space/CR/LF/tab allowances and may be rejected by R4 validators that apply the regex as a full-string lexical rule. Serializer-specific character rules may impose additional restrictions.

findings.narrativeMd: `string.value` changed from the R4 regex `[ \r\n\t\S]+` to the R6 regex `^[\s\S]+$`. This broadens the primitive lexical space to any non-empty sequence under normal regex semantics. Existing R4 values are not expected to fail R6 validation because of this change, but new R6 values can be outside what older R4 validators or generated schemas accept.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: For R4-to-R6 migration, this is not an old-valid/new-invalid change. For R6-to-R4 conversion, values containing characters accepted only by the R6 regex may fail R4 validation or require lossless preservation outside the primitive value, such as a conversion error, profile-specific policy, or extension-based workaround. Strict parsers and code generators that embed the old regex are the most likely runtime failure point.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Update validators and generated schema artifacts to use the R6 regex for R6 content. Cross-version conversion tests should include strings with ordinary text, whitespace-only strings, empty strings, max-length boundary cases, and uncommon whitespace/control characters. Down-converters to R4 should either reject non-R4-lexical values with an explicit error or apply a documented, potentially lossy normalization policy only if the receiving workflow permits it.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The change is mostly backward-compatible in the R4-to-R6 direction because it broadens accepted values. The unavoidable compatibility gap is reverse-direction: once R6 permits values that R4 did not, no purely structural R4 representation can preserve all such values while satisfying the old regex. Guidance and warnings are the least disruptive mitigation.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: Confirm intended regex matching semantics against official R6 narrative or validator behavior if this finding will drive automated conversion rules. Some serializers may reject certain control characters before FHIR regex validation is reached.

freshReview.narrativeMd: The affected path is only `string.value`. R4 used `[ \r\n\t\S]+`; R6 uses `^[\s\S]+$`; cardinality, type, and `maxLength` remain unchanged. Under normal whole-value primitive validation, the R6 regex is broader: it still requires a non-empty value but admits whitespace/control characters that the R4 character class may exclude. That can matter when converting R6 content back to R4 or when an R4-era validator is reused for R6 content, but it does not make an R4-valid `string` invalid in R6 and does not change the generated element path or API shape. For an R4-to-R6 break review, this is not a meaningful compatibility problem.
keyEvidence: Fresh-review framework applied: element-level findings are assessed only at the affected path and direct downstream behavior.
Existing report finding `string:VALUE_CONSTRAINT:string.value:regex-broadened` identifies a local regex change on `string.value`.
R4 `StructureDefinition-string.json` has `string.value` regex `[ \r\n\t\S]+`, cardinality `0..1`, type `http://hl7.org/fhirpath/System.String`, and `maxLength` 1048576.
R6 `StructureDefinition-string.json` has `string.value` regex `^[\s\S]+$`, with the same cardinality, type, and `maxLength` 1048576.
R4 maturity data and StructureDefinition extensions show `string` is normative with normative version 4.0.0.
freshReview.fmmEffect: Normative status raises the review burden for true R4-to-R6 breaks, so the regex change was checked carefully. It does not turn this widening into a concern because the direct compatibility issue is reverse-direction only.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: R6-to-R4 loss: an R6 string containing characters admitted only by `^[\s\S]+$` may not satisfy the older R4 regex, but there is no old-valid/new-invalid R4-to-R6 instance break and no runtime/API/codegen path change.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: No less-breaking base R6 design is needed for R4-to-R6 compatibility because R6 widened the lexical constraint. Keeping the R4 regex would improve down-conversion compatibility but would preserve the older exclusions and conflict with the apparent R6 goal of accepting any non-empty string value.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: Partially agree with the existing impact and alternative judgment: it correctly treats this as no hard R4-to-R6 break and finds no less-breaking R6 base design necessary, but I would not carry forward a Medium overall concern for this fresh review because the practical issue is uncommon and reverse-direction.

checkedNoMaterialChange.notesMd: Canonical URL, id, name, status, kind, type, abstract flag, and specialization derivation are stable. The direct base change is inherited/base-infrastructure scope.
Both snapshots contain the same local element paths: `string`, `string.id`, `string.extension`, and `string.value`.
`string.id` and `string.value` still use `http://hl7.org/fhirpath/System.String`, and `string.extension` still uses `Extension`.
`string` has no local Reference elements or targetProfiles.
No local terminology binding is present on `string` in either StructureDefinition.

No local `string`-specific invariant was added or removed. Inherited `Element`/`Extension` constraint wording and XPath changes are out of scope; the local regex change is reported separately as a value constraint.
No fixed value, pattern value, or default value is present locally in either version.
`maxLength` remains 1048576. The regex changed and is covered by finding `string:VALUE_CONSTRAINT:string.value:regex-broadened`.
No local slicing was introduced on `string`. Inherited `Element.extension` slicing belongs to the base artifact analysis.
The root definition remains 'A sequence of Unicode characters'. The size comment was clarified without changing the computable `maxLength`; full narrative pages were not available locally.
`string.id` and `string.value` retain `xmlAttr` representation; no local JSON/XML shape change was found.
The broadened regex creates a limited R6-to-R4 representability risk for unusual characters; no other local reverse-representability issue was found.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: Maximum-size comment clarified from 1MB to 1,048,576 characters
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: The computable `string.value.maxLength` remains 1048576 in both R4 and R6, so this wording change does not alter validation by itself.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Documentation and UI messages should prefer the R6 wording because it is more precise: the limit is expressed as 1024*1024 characters rather than the ambiguous phrase `1MB`.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: R6 adds type-characteristics metadata for string
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: R6 adds `structuredefinition-type-characteristics` extension values `can-bind`, `has-length`, and `do-translations`. These are metadata about the datatype and do not add or remove instance elements or change local cardinalities.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Code generators or authoring tools that consume StructureDefinition metadata may expose new capabilities for binding, length handling, or translation support on `string`; this should be additive for instance validation.

followUpDependencies.reasonMd: R6 routes `string` through `PrimitiveType` and `DataType`; any class-hierarchy, code-generation, or inherited-element consequences should be assessed in the base datatype reports.
Inherited `ele-1` wording and XPath removal appear in the `string` snapshot but are base `Element` changes, not local `string` changes.

analysisLimitations.descriptionMd: No official R4-to-R6 diff, ballot note, or Jira rationale was available locally for the regex change.
analysisLimitations.whatWouldResolveItMd: An official diff or change note explaining the regex update would confirm whether the intended impact is exactly to broaden the lexical space.

analysisLimitations.descriptionMd: The practical set of values accepted by the R4 regex depends on the validator's regex dialect, Unicode handling, and whether matching is anchored or whole-string by convention.
analysisLimitations.whatWouldResolveItMd: Testing representative R4 and R6 validators against uncommon whitespace/control characters would quantify the real compatibility gap.

analysisLimitations.descriptionMd: The local R6 StructureDefinition narrative for `string` is placeholder generated text, so this report relies on computable StructureDefinition fields rather than full narrative datatype guidance.
analysisLimitations.whatWouldResolveItMd: Comparing the official R4 and current R6 datatype narrative pages would improve confidence in semantic and serializer guidance.

analysisLimitations.descriptionMd: No terminology expansion was performed because `string` has no local terminology binding in either StructureDefinition.
analysisLimitations.whatWouldResolveItMd: No terminology input is expected to change this report unless a profile-specific `string` binding is introduced outside the core datatype.
